channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro precisa recuperar espaço na direita não-bolsonarista e entre independentes, avaliam aliados após Quaest
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro needs to regain support among non-Bolsonarist right-wing voters and independents after losing trust due to his proximity to banker Daniel Vorcaro. Although he retains strong backing from Bolsonarist hardliners (91%), his standing among moderate voters is eroding, with undecided voters rising from 3% to 11%. The Quaest poll indicates he remains the PL’s only viable candidate to challenge Lula in a potential runoff.

item.title: Maioria dos eleitores avalia que Flávio não é mais moderado que a família Bolsonaro, aponta Genial/Quaest
item.description: A majority of voters (54%) believe Flávio Bolsonaro is no longer more moderate than his family, up four points since June. His image as a 'moderate Bolsonaro' has declined from 39% in April to 29% currently, while 57% of Brazilians know him and would not vote for him. Additionally, 46% fear the return of the Bolsonaros to power, compared to 38% who fear Lula’s re-election.

item.title: Áudio: Senado aprova MP do Frete Mínimo, que beneficia caminhoneiros
item.description: The Senate approved Provisional Measure 1.343/2026, which mandates the registration of road cargo transport operations and strengthens enforcement of the minimum freight floor, benefiting truck drivers. The measure, now headed for presidential sanction, also includes a pardon for drivers who blocked roads after the 2022 elections, approved with amendments by lawmakers.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: para 45%, Michelle acertou em gravar vídeo contra Flávio; 38% consideram erro
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll shows 45% of voters believed Michelle Bolsonaro was right to publicly disclose her disagreement with Flávio Bolsonaro, while 38% thought it was a mistake. 17% did not know or declined to answer.

item.title: O eleitorado que puxou a aprovação de Lula ao mais alto patamar do ano, segundo pesquisa
item.description: Lula reached 48% approval in July 2026, his highest level this year and the highest since December 2025, with steady growth since April. The largest gain came from the highest-income group (above five minimum wages), which saw a 6-point approval increase and a 6-point disapproval drop in one month. Young voters (16-34) added 5 points in approval and reduced disapproval by 4, while the South — despite remaining the most critical region — rose 4 points in approval and fell 5 in disapproval since June.

item.title: Cid Gomes aparece à frente na disputa pelo Senado no Ceará
item.description: Senator Cid Gomes (PSB-CE) leads the Senate reelection race in Ceará with 26% voter intention, according to a Real Time Big Data poll, closely followed by Capitão Wagner (União Brasil) at 22%, within the margin of error. Gomes decided to run again at the request of President Lula (PT), while Wagner tops a second scenario without Gomes, showing strong competitiveness between the two main contenders.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 42% concordam mais com Michelle em briga com Flávio
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll shows 42% of respondents side more with Michelle Bolsonaro after her public dispute with Flávio Bolsonaro, versus 18% supporting the senator. The conflict, stemming from disagreements over the PL’s electoral slate in Ceará, led Michelle to resign from PL Women’s leadership and sparked divided opinions: 45% believe she was right to release the video, while 38% think she was wrong.

item.title: Flávio é rejeitado por 57% e Lula, por 50%, diz Quaest
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has a 57% rejection rate, while President Lula (PT) has 50%, according to a Quaest poll released on July 15, 2026. The survey, conducted between July 10–13 with 2,004 respondents across 120 municipalities, has a 2-point margin of error and was funded by Banco Genial in partnership with Globo Group.

item.title: A vitória da ala política do PL sobre o ‘bolsonarismo raiz’
item.description: The selection of Carlos Portinho (PL-RJ) for the Senate race represented a victory for the political wing of the PL over the 'bolsonarism raiz' faction, defeating the Bolsonaro family's favored candidate, Carlos Jordy (PL-RJ). The state party directory, backed by over 30 inland mayors, prioritized electoral viability to bolster the presidential bid of Flávio Bolsonaro and the gubernatorial campaign of Douglas Ruas, favoring pragmatic alliances over pure ideological alignment.

item.title: Trump transforma autonomia do Brasil em delito comercial, diz jornal britânico sobre tarifas
item.description: The British newspaper The Guardian claims that Donald Trump is using threats of commercial tariffs against Brazil to undermine the country’s autonomy, particularly regarding digital platform regulation and countering democratic misinformation. The editorial criticizes the U.S. stance that it should have jurisdiction over Brazil’s information space, noting that Brazil’s Supreme Court held social media platforms accountable for content linked to the 2023 far-right coup attempt led by Bolsonaro. It links this trade pressure to the amplification of bolsonarism in Washington.

item.title: Governo Lula é aprovado por 48% e desaprovado por 47%, diz Quaest
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government registered 48% approval and 47% disapproval in a Quaest poll released on July 15, 2026, marking the first positive approval balance since December 2024. The survey, conducted from July 10–13, 2026, interviewed 2,004 people across 120 municipalities, with a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level. The study, funded by Banco Genial at a cost of R$433,255.92, is registered with the TSE under BR-07181/2026.

item.title: Lula e Flávio zeram desgastes e cenário é o mesmo de oito meses atrás
item.description: Lula has largely erased the wear and tear from the first half of the year, regaining his lead in electoral polls after a period when his disapproval exceeded approval and analysts questioned his frontrunner status. Flávio Bolsonaro has returned to the voter intention levels he had in December, when his father, Jair Bolsonaro, pointed to him as a potential presidential successor. The current electoral scenario resembles that of eight months ago, with Lula recovered and Flávio stabilized.

item.title: Depois de censurar, Nunes Marques quer ‘premiar’ pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: In June, Justice Kassio Nunes Marques of the TSE censored an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll on Flávio Bolsonaro at the senator's request, claiming non-neutral questions, despite constitutional bans on political censorship. In July, he proposed a regulation to 'reward' polling firms whose estimates most closely match official election results, drawing criticism for conflating polling with prediction and attempting to repair the court's image after the censorship backlash.

item.title: Por que o "selo" para pesquisas de Nunes Marques é um absurdo completo
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques proposed an 'electoral accuracy seal' to reward polling institutes whose results come closest to actual election outcomes — an idea widely ridiculed as absurd and statistically baseless by experts like Luciana Chong of Datafolha and Antônio Lavareda, who stress that polls are snapshots, not predictions. The move is seen as a smokescreen to shield the minister after his failed attempt to block legitimate Atlas Intel polls showing Flávio Bolsonaro's declining support among voters.

item.title: A melhora na aprovação de Lula, segundo a Quaest
item.description: The Quaest poll released in July 2026 shows that President Lula's approval rating has surpassed disapproval for the first time since December 2024, with 48% approving and 47% disapproving — a technical tie within the two-point margin of error. In April, disapproval stood at 52% and approval at 43%, marking a notable improvement. While the approval-disapproval gap is statistically tied, direct evaluation of his government shows 36% positive and 36% negative ratings, also tied, with 26% rating it as regular.

item.title: Percepção de melhora da economia explica melhora na avaliação do governo Lula, indica Quaest
item.description: The Quaest poll shows 48% of Brazilians approve of Lula's government, compared to 47% who disapprove, in a technical tie, but with approval exceeding disapproval for the first time since 2024. Improved economic perception, particularly driven by the Desenrola 2.0 program, is cited as the main factor behind the decline in disapproval and rise in approval, with 39 million Brazilians having accessed the program and 35% reporting a significant income increase. Additionally, 69% of voters support ending the 6x1 work schedule, with 53% saying they would spend more time with family if implemented.

item.title: Os números da disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno, segundo a Quaest
item.description: The Quaest/Genial poll released on July 15, 2026 shows President Lula (PT) leading Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a hypothetical second-round runoff with 45% to 37%, an eight-point advantage. Lula also leads against other simulated opponents: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) at 36%, Romeu Zema (Novo) at 35%, and Renan Santos (Missão) at 33%. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters between July 10 and 13, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Lula tem 45% contra 37% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz Quaest
item.description: According to a Quaest poll released on July 15, 2026, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leads in a hypothetical second-round runoff with 45% voting intentions, compared to 37% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). The margin of error is 2 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. Flávio Bolsonaro is the most rejected candidate at 57%, while Lula’s rejection stands at 50%.

item.title: Lula merece mais quatro anos como presidente? Veja o que diz a nova pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 45% of Brazilians believe Lula deserves another four-year term, while 51% disagree — marking the first time in a year that re-election support has risen above the previous 39%. Government approval also reached 48%, surpassing disapproval (47%) for the first time in 12 months, driven by gains among independents and non-Lulist left voters. Lula leads all tested second-round scenarios, including against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with 45% voting intention.

item.title: Quaest: 62% consideram que caso Jaques Wagner impacta negativamente a campanha de Lula
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 62% of Brazilians believe the investigation into Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) and Banco Master harms Lula's re-election campaign, with 37% seeing it as very negative and 25% as somewhat negative. 61% think Wagner acted improperly, and 43% view the case as an institutional issue for Lula's government, not just personal. Nevertheless, 54% of the population says they are unaware of the investigation.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: rejeição de Flávio vai a 57% após vídeo de Michelle e viagem aos EUA
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released this Wednesday shows that 57% of Brazilians reject Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), up one percentage point from last month. Rejection of Lula (PT) fell from 53% to 50% over the same period, narrowing the gap between them to seven percentage points. The rise in Flávio's rejection is tied to revelations about his links to banker Daniel Vorcaro, videos from Michelle Bolsonaro accusing him of mistreatment, and his U.S. trip where he defended Pix and criticized tariffs on Brazilian goods.

item.title: Intenção de votos de direita não bolsonarista em Flávio despenca
item.description: Non-bolsonarist right-wing voting intention for Flávio Bolsonaro dropped from 90% in March to 74% in the Genial/Quaest poll, while bolsonarist support fell from 97% to 91%. The decline is linked to Bolsonaro’s involvement with Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master, in funding a film about Jair Bolsonaro, revealed in May. The article is subscriber-only, requiring registration for full access.

item.title: Quaest: envolvimento de Wagner no Master atrapalha campanha de Lula
item.description: The involvement of Jaques Wagner, former Lula government leader in the Senate, in the Master case negatively impacts Lula's campaign for 37% of Brazilians, according to the Genial/Quaest poll. Another 25% say the impact is only partial. The story is subscriber-only and highlights potential damage to Lula's image.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 45% acreditam que Michelle acertou ao divulgar vídeo com críticas a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Genial/Quaest poll shows 45% of voters believe Michelle Bolsonaro was right to release a video accusing her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro of mistreatment and disrespect, while 38% think she was wrong. Furthermore, 42% tend to side with Michelle in the family dispute, versus 18% supporting Flávio, and 58% find her allegations at least partially true.

item.title: Quaest: depois de 19 meses, aprovação de Lula supera desaprovação
item.description: For the first time since December 2024, President Lula's approval (48%) exceeds his disapproval (47%), according to a Quaest poll. The technical tie reflects a one-point gain in approval and a corresponding drop in disapproval compared to the June survey.

item.title: Aprovação do governo Lula cresce em redutos considerados bolsonaristas
item.description: President Lula's approval grew significantly in traditionally Bolsonarist strongholds, rising from 35% to 41% among those earning more than five minimum wages. While national approval increased only from 47% to 48%, disapproval in this group dropped from 60% to 54%, according to the Genial/Quaest poll.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 61% veem erro de Jaques Wagner no caso Master, e 43% apontam 'questão institucional' do governo Lula
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 61% of Brazilians believe Jaques Wagner acted wrongly in the Master case, with 43% viewing it as an institutional issue of the Lula government. However, 54% of voters say they were unaware of the investigations, and only 31% claim to be well informed.

item.title: Governo Lula é aprovado por 48% dos brasileiros, contra 47% que o desaprovam, mostra Genial/Quaest
item.description: Lula's government has 48% approval and 47% disapproval, marking the first time since December 2024 that approval exceeds disapproval. Lula leads all second-round scenarios, with 45% against 37% for Flávio Bolsonaro, 36% for Ronaldo Caiado, 35% for Romeu Zema, and 33% for Renan Santos. In the first round, Lula has 40% of voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 28%.

item.title: Quaest: Lula lidera com 45% contra 37% de Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno
item.description: Lula leads with 45% voting intention against 37% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, according to Quaest poll. The president’s advantage grew from 4 points in June to 8 points now, indicating weakness in Bolsonaro’s campaign, particularly after the Michelle Bolsonaro video controversy. In all four runoff scenarios tested, Lula would be re-elected, with the narrowest margin against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Quaest: após vídeos em que Michelle Bolsonaro diz ter sido humilhada por Flávio, 42% concordam mais com ela e 18% com o senador
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 42% of respondents side more with Michelle Bolsonaro after she released videos claiming Flávio Bolsonaro humiliated her, compared to 18% for Flávio. 45% believe Michelle did right by making the dispute public, and 49% had already seen the videos. The incident is seen as damaging Flávio’s support among right-wing voters, according to Quaest’s director.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 48% aprovam o governo Lula; 47% desaprovam
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 48% of Brazilians approve of President Lula's government, while 47% disapprove — marking the first time approval numerically exceeds disapproval, though within the margin of error. The result reflects a highly polarized electorate, with Lula’s government maintaining a fragile balance in public support.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Lula mantém tendência de subida e abre 8 pontos sobre Flávio
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows President Lula (PT) maintaining an upward trend in voter intentions, leading Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) by eight percentage points in a simulated runoff for the 2026 elections. In the first-round scenario, Lula’s advantage expands to 12 points. The results highlight Lula’s consistent lead in the electoral simulations released.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Aprovação de Lula vai a 48% e supera numericamente a desaprovação pela 1ª vez
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on July 15 shows President Lula’s approval rating at 48%, surpassing disapproval at 47% for the first time in 18 months. However, the lead falls within the poll’s two-point margin of error, making it a technical tie. Lula also leads in 2026 election voting intentions, expanding his advantage in potential second-round matchups against rivals such as Flávio Bolsonaro, Romeu Zema, Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos.

item.title: Lula tem 62% e Flávio Bolsonaro 21% no Ceará, diz RealTime Big Data
item.description: In Ceará, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leads with 62% of voting intentions, followed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 22%, according to a RealTime Big Data poll. In a hypothetical runoff, Lula rises to 66% and Bolsonaro to 26%. The survey also shows Bolsonaro has the highest rejection rate in the state at 60%, while Lula has 26% rejection and 68% approval of his administration.

item.title: Problema com indígenas na COP30 foi pontual, diz Sonia Guajajara
item.description: Sonia Guajajara, federal deputy and former Minister of Indigenous Peoples, stated that the protests by the Munduruku indigenous people in the Blue Zone of COP30 in November 2025 were a 'punctual issue' and that the federal government's relationship with the indigenous movement remains normal. She emphasized that during her tenure (2023-2026), 20 indigenous territories were homologated — six more than projected in the 2022 transition — and that the government advanced in dismantling illegal mining in Munduruku territory, despite constraints from the Marco Temporal.

item.title: Sonia Guajajara tem 25 cocares e diz que já teve 1 furtado
item.description: Deputy Sonia Guajajara (Psol-SP) reveals she owns about 25 headdresses (cocares) stored in her residences in Brasília, São Paulo, and Maranhão, after having one stolen. She uses the headdresses respectfully in rituals, mobilizations, and ceremonies, always honoring the cultural origin of each group. Guajajara also condemns the illegal online sale of headdresses, calling for stricter enforcement to prevent 'superfilling' and misuse of these sacred items.

item.title: PL corre contra o tempo e quer definir vice de Flávio até a próxima semana
item.description: PL leaders are racing against time to select a vice-presidential running mate for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket by mid-next week, aiming to generate political momentum for his struggling presidential pre-candidacy. Clarissa Tércio of the PP has resurfaced as a top contender due to her identity as a woman from Northeast Brazil, though her evangelical faith raises concerns among leaders who prefer a candidate closer to Catholicism. The final decision hinges on securing alignment from the PP and União Brasil, both of which have recently signaled neutrality in the presidential race.

item.title: Sidônio fica até o final do governo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has decided that Minister Sidônio Palmeira will remain in office until the end of his term, ruling out any possibility of his departure to support the 2026 electoral campaign. The decision aims to prevent the use of government marketing for electoral purposes, preserving the separation between administration and campaign activities. The information is exclusive to subscribers of the outlet that published the report.

item.title: Presidente da Abimaq acredita em novo tarifaço de 25% sobre produtos brasileiros
item.description: José Velloso, president of Abimaq, believes the U.S. may impose a new 25% tariff on 21% of Brazilian exports, including machinery and equipment, despite the Lula government denying any 'tariff hike'. He views the situation as unpredictable due to Donald Trump's stance and divergence between Itamaraty and the presidency.

item.title: Por que carta de Bolsonaro virou alvo de Moraes enquanto Lula também divulgou cartas da prisão
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes barred Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after the latter’s letter was released, citing risks to institutional order. In 2018, Lula’s letters were disseminated during his presidential campaign while imprisoned, without comparable judicial restrictions. The key distinction lies in context: Bolsonaro faces charges related to an alleged coup attempt, whereas Lula was serving time for passive corruption and money laundering.

item.title: Bolsonaro tem até esta 4ª para esclarecer descumprimento de cautelares
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered Bolsonaro's defense to respond by Wednesday (July 15) regarding a possible breach of precautionary measures after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro shared a letter from the former president on social media, naming him as spokesperson in the 2026 election race. The ruling also suspended Flávio's visits to his father for 90 days and referred the case to the Electoral Prosecutor's Office to investigate premature campaigning. Moraes labeled Flávio a repeat offender in violating court orders.

item.title: Com iminência de novo tarifaço, governo Lula vê pressão sobre eleição
item.description: The Lula government believes a potential new U.S. tariff on Brazilian exports, possibly at 25%, is politically and ideologically motivated to influence Brazil’s 2026 presidential election. It views the move as interference, especially after U.S. courts struck down prior tariffs as illegal and amid an ongoing investigation into practices like Pix. The Planalto argues that Brazil’s technical objections are being ignored, suggesting the tariff serves external interests in Brazil’s domestic electoral contest.

item.title: Dia D das tarifas: EUA chega a decisão sobre tarifaço nesta quarta
item.description: The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) will decide this Wednesday (July 15) whether to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian products, following an investigation launched in July 2025. Despite a U.S. trade surplus, Washington alleging unfair trade practices. The Lula government is preparing for the possibility of tariffs, as negotiations have failed to produce an agreement.

item.title: TSE libera campanha do governo Lula sobre bets no defeso eleitoral
item.description: The president of the TSE, Minister Nunes Marques, authorized the Lula government to disseminate institutional advertising about the risks of online betting during the electoral blackout period (July to October 2026). The campaign, named 'National Campaign for Prevention of Harms from Online Betting', aims to inform the public about mental health impacts and guide them on warning signs and SUS services. The minister emphasized there is no electoral intent, stating the action complies with the prohibition on abusive use of public resources.

item.title: Pesquisa interna do PL desanima grupo de Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio
item.description: Internal PL polls in Rio de Janeiro show Flávio Bolsonaro technically tied with Lula, raising concerns among party leaders, as the state is considered the historical heartland of bolsonarismo. The result is seen as a warning sign for the senator’s presidential campaign.

item.title: A multa que Flávio Bolsonaro terá de pagar caso carta do pai seja considerada irregular
item.description: The campaign of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) could face a fine of up to R$ 25,000 if the dissemination of a letter written by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is deemed premature electoral propaganda by the TSE. The minimum fine under electoral law is R$ 5,000. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Governo Lula avalia que tarifaço só será negociado após as eleições, caso taxa seja confirmada pelos EUA
item.description: The Lula administration believes that any potential U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods will only be negotiated after the 2026 elections, as the U.S. may wait to see whether Flávio Bolsonaro or Lula wins, given their diametrically opposed stances on trade concessions. The USTR decision could be announced starting this Wednesday, and the Planalto will await the list of affected products before crafting a response, avoiding premature actions. Flávio Bolsonaro’s request for a delay was seen as a move that benefits Lula’s position.

item.title: Após queixa de Alcolumbre, articuladores de Lula tentam conter Boulos e bancada do PT em embate sobre fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Lula’s political allies are attempting to contain pressure from Minister Guilherme Boulos and the PT caucus in the Chamber to vote on ending the 6x1 work schedule, following a formal complaint by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who opposes the proposal. The clash unfolds amid delicate political negotiations over labor reform, as the government seeks to avoid institutional rupture while keeping its base mobilized.

item.title: Rumble afirma que AGU mudou versão para defender Moraes
item.description: Rumble and Trump Media & Technology Group told a Florida court that the AGU changed its position on the reach of Brazilian judicial decisions by Minister Alexandre de Moraes to try to dismiss the case in the U.S. The companies claim that in June 2025, Brazil’s Justice Department told the U.S. Department of Justice that Brazilian rulings have effect only domestically and must be enforced via international cooperation channels, but now the AGU argues Moraes’ orders are sovereign acts immune from U.S. scrutiny. The suit does not challenge the validity of Moraes’ decisions in Brazil, but whether they can impose obligations on U.S. entities without U.S. government authorization or diplomatic mechanisms.

item.title: Após convencer Cid Gomes, PT busca alianças no Ceará e negocia 2ª vaga ao Senado, diante de disputa acirrada com Ciro
item.description: The PT in Ceará is seeking to define a second Senate candidate for Governor Elmano de Freitas's ticket, already confirmed with Cid Gomes (PSB), to strengthen the campaign amid a tight race against Ciro Gomes (PSDB). Names under discussion include Luizianne Lins (Rede), Eunício Oliveira (MDB), Chiquinho Feitosa (Republicanos), and potential PSD or PP representatives. Cid Gomes' candidacy was secured after a meeting with Lula, aiming to create a political counterpoint to Ciro and broaden state-level alliances.
